name: Soundproofing Strategies for Attached ADU Additions in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County address soundproofing between the main home and the new ADU?
mainEntity.text: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County address soundproofing between the main home and the new ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sound privacy is one of the most common complaints when attached ADUs share walls or floors with the main home. Los Angeles County does not always mandate high levels of acoustic separation, but experienced ADU additions contractors treat soundproofing as a design priority. They typically start with insulated separation walls using mineral wool or high‑density fiberglass. To further reduce noise transmission, resilient channels or sound isolation clips can decouple drywall from framing, limiting vibration. Sound‑rated drywall or double layers of standard drywall with staggered seams provide additional mass. Floor and ceiling assemblies between levels may incorporate acoustic underlayment, insulation, and suspended ceilings to dampen footfall noise. All penetrations, such as electrical boxes and plumbing, require careful sealing with acoustical caulk or putty pads. Solid‑core doors with good weatherstripping at any connecting openings between the units are essential. Locating bedrooms away from noisy areas like living rooms or kitchens on the opposite side also helps. Discuss your expectations for noise with your contractor early and ask them to outline specific materials and assemblies they propose. Proper soundproofing is easier and cheaper to build in from the start than to retrofit after move‑in.
acceptedAnswer.description: Contractors improve soundproofing between an attached ADU and the main home using insulated walls, resilient channels, sound-rated drywall, and solid-core doors. Planning wall locations, mechanical runs, and floor assemblies with noise in mind is essential to give both units privacy and rental-ready acoustic separation.
